name: Razorfen
summary: Across southern Kalimdor, Razorfen's quilboar defend their thorn-walled homes. Their strongholds span the southern Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, where their faith and power run deep.

sections.title: The Thorns of Agamaggan
sections.body: Razorfen's thorned brambles reach back to the War of the Ancients. Legend says they rose where Agamaggan, the giant boar Ancient, fell fighting the Burning Legion ten thousand years ago. His blood entered the earth, and vast vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns grew there. The quilboar, his descendants, have lived among these defenses ever since.

sections.title: The Razorfen Tribe
sections.body: Razorfen's quilboar are among the most aggressive and firmly rooted of their kind. They build their communities among the vast briars instead of scattering into open warrens. From these strongholds, they defend their ancestral land against neighboring tauren tribes, Horde settlements in the Barrens, and any outsider who enters their holy grounds.

sections.title: A Divided Citadel
sections.body: Razorfen's two bastions hold different places in quilboar life. Razorfen Kraul is the tribe's main stronghold and military camp, guarded by shamans and huntresses. Farther south at the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen Downs is their traditional capital, sacred ancestral city, and burial ground of quilboar elders. A deeper necromantic corruption now shadows the city and threatens the surrounding lands.

faq.answer: Razorfen names a prominent quilboar tribe of the southern Barrens and its settlements, woven through massive briar labyrinths. They include Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs.

faq.q: Where did the giant thorns come from?
faq.answer: Legend says the giant thorns grew from the blood and remains of Agamaggan, the Great Boar. He fell fighting the Burning Legion during the ancient War of the Ancients, and thorned tendrils rose where his blood struck the earth.

faq.q: What is the difference between Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs?
faq.answer: Razorfen Kraul is the tribe's living city and main stronghold, filled with warriors and geomancers. Farther south toward Thousand Needles, Razorfen Downs is the ancestral burial ground and sacred resting place of quilboar elders.

faq.q: Why are the quilboar hostile to everyone?
faq.answer: The quilboar see the Barrens and its great briars as a divine birthright from Agamaggan. They regard outside races, especially the expanding Horde, as thieves invading their holy ground.
Razorfen's vast thorn networks lie in the far south of the Barrens, along the high cliffs descending into the salt flats and river canyon of Thousand Needles.

faq.q: What kind of magic do the Razorfen quilboar use?
faq.answer: Razorfen quilboar traditionally practice geomancy, an earth and nature magic that calls on stone and thorn. Recent developments within Razorfen Downs reveal alarming incursions of dark necromantic arts.

angles.text: Razorfen quilboar have fought tauren hunting bands and settlements across the Barrens for generations. Their eradication is a matter of homeland security.
Control of the southern Barrens is critical to Horde logistics. Razorfen raiders repeatedly harass caravans traveling between Mulgore, Crossroads, and the southern frontier.
The briars of Razorfen grew from the sacrifice of the Ancient Agamaggan. As a druid, you have reason for deep concern when such a sacred site is desecrated and corrupted.
Razorfen geomancers use crude elemental rites to shape the spirits of earth and stone. As a shaman, you must attend to their work in seeking balance.
